name: What Delays a Garage Addition Project?

mainEntity.name: What site conditions most often delay garage addition projects in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What site conditions most often delay garage addition projects in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Garage addition projects are often delayed by conditions the homeowner cannot see from the street. Common problems include unexpected grading needs, unstable or soft soil, poor drainage, buried utility lines, limited equipment access, and property boundary issues. In Los Angeles County, permit corrections can also add time if the initial drawings do not match local zoning or building requirements. Inspection delays may slow the project further if the schedule is tight or the city has a backlog. Older homes can create extra complications when existing structures, drainage, or electrical systems do not match current standards. The best way to reduce delay risk is to do a detailed site review before signing a contract and to ask the contractor how they handle unknown conditions. A careful preconstruction phase usually saves time later, even if it takes a little longer to start.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common delays come from poor soil, slope, drainage problems, utility conflicts, permit corrections, and inspection scheduling. Hidden site issues can force redesigns or change orders after work has already started, especially on older lots.
